summary: Iteration 16 (per-user module access control) tested end-to-end. Backend: 12/12 pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration16_access.py — restricted user with access=[dashboard,projects] gets 200 on /api/dashboard & /api/projects and 403 {detail:'no_access'} on /api/ledger, /api/partner/overview, /api/investments, /api/properties, /api/personal-loans, /api/feasibility; admin PUT /api/admin/users/{uid}/access grants partners+investments and both endpoints flip to 200 instantly WITHOUT re-login (DB re-read per request); revoke flips them back to 403; invalid module name 'bogus' silently filtered on PUT; empty access=[] blocks even /api/dashboard (403) but /api/auth/me still works and returns access:[]; admin /api/auth/me returns full MODULES list; legacy user doc with no 'access' field logs in and still gets full module access (403-free) + /auth/me returns all 7 modules — matches server.py get_current_user normalization at line 125-126. Frontend: admin Access UI verified — admin row shows NO 'Access' button (admin not in own-row toggle), non-admin rows have access-toggle-<uid> that expands access-row-<uid> with 7 pills access-<uid>-{dashboard,projects,feasibility,partners,loans,investments,properties}; clicking Save fires PUT, shows 'Access updated' toast, closes row, and pills persist across reload (verified by text-gold class). Enforcement in Require guard works: as restricted user with access=[dashboard,projects,partners,investments], direct visit to /partners LOADS; /properties and /feasibility REDIRECT to /. After revoke to [dashboard] only, /partners also redirects to /.

ui_bugs.component: Layout sidebar/mobile nav after fresh login
ui_bugs.issue: After /api/auth/login succeeds, the sidebar renders EMPTY (zero nav items) for non-admin users because POST /api/auth/login's response payload does NOT include 'access' — AuthContext.login() calls setUser(r.data) with that payload, so user.access is undefined and navItems filter `(user?.access||[]).includes(n.mod)` matches nothing. A full page reload fixes it because AuthProvider's useEffect calls /api/auth/me which DOES include access. Reproduced: login as restricted user → sidebar blank + no mobile tabs; press F5 → sidebar correctly shows Dashboard, Projects, Partner Ledger, Investments. Admin unaffected (early-return admin branch doesn't need access list).

integration_issues.issue: Non-admin user is stranded on an empty dashboard with no sidebar links immediately after login until they refresh. Nav sidebar is empty because login response omits 'access'.

action_items: In /app/backend/server.py @app.post('/api/auth/login') return payload, add 'access': user.get('access') if isinstance(user.get('access'), list) else list(MODULES) (and MODULES if role=='admin') so AuthContext.login() populates user.access immediately and the sidebar renders without a reload. Same fix likely needed in /api/auth/google/session response for consistency.

Cleanup: previous testing left 'access.test@example.com' (uid 6ad6c61172a34f47ff085a37, access=['dashboard','investments']) in db.users — main agent should delete via DELETE /api/admin/users/{uid} or mongo (prior iteration note said this was already deleted; it isn't).
critical_code_review_comments: Login response payload drift vs /auth/me: login returns {id,email,name,picture,role,status} but /auth/me adds 'access'. The frontend treats both as the same user object (AuthContext.login does setUser(r.data) and AuthProvider useEffect does the same from /me). Keep them in sync — missing fields silently break downstream UI (see nav-empty bug above).

server.py MODULE_PATHS uses startswith prefix matching — note that /api/loans maps to 'projects' (project loans) while /api/personal-loans maps to 'loans' (private loans). The ordering has /api/personal-loans listed first which is correct, but a developer adding /api/loan-anything-else could accidentally bind to 'projects'. Consider a stricter path match or explicit router-level dependency.

module_access_middleware re-reads the user doc from Mongo on every gated request to make grant/revoke instant — this is correct for the stated UX guarantee but doubles DB round-trips vs trusting the JWT. For high-traffic deployments add a short TTL in-memory cache keyed by uid.

Partner Ledger UI calls /api/ledger, /api/partner/overview, /api/partner-report/{name}, /api/partners-list — all four are mapped (ledger→partners, partner-report→partners, partner/overview→partners). /api/partners-list is NOT in MODULE_PATHS, so a restricted user could enumerate partner names via it. Add ('/api/partners-list','partners') to MODULE_PATHS. Note: grep confirms /api/partners-list exists at ~line 1200s and is called from frontend partner autocomplete.
server.py is now 2044 lines — split into modules (auth, admin, access, investments, etoro, dashboard, report) remains strongly recommended per prior iterations.

rca of the issue: The sidebar-empty-after-login bug: /api/auth/login response payload lacks 'access' field (unlike /api/auth/me). Frontend AuthContext.login does setUser(r.data). Layout.jsx navItems filters by (user?.access||[]).includes(n.mod) — with access undefined → zero items. On page reload, AuthProvider's useEffect hits /api/auth/me which DOES return 'access' (added via get_current_user normalization line 123-126) → sidebar populates. Fix: in login() around line 416, change return to include 'access': list(MODULES) if role=='admin' else (user.get('access') if isinstance(user.get('access'), list) else list(MODULES)).
